export const meta = {
  name: 'globe-writers-3',
  description: 'Write the prototype section, assemble research/globe/README.md from the fragments with a consistent decision numbering and a method section, then run an adversarial critic that fixes small faults',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Prototype section', detail: 'section 11 from the prototype evidence' },
    { title: 'Assemble', detail: 'README from fragments; renumber D30-D40 to D31-D41; add section 16; link check' },
    { title: 'Critic', detail: 'completeness, rules, numbers, links; small fixes applied' },
  ],
}

const REPO = '/home/user/RoofingApp'
const EVID = REPO + '/research/globe/validation-evidence/'
const SCRATCH = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad'
const FRAG = SCRATCH + '/readme-sections/'
const README = REPO + '/research/globe/README.md'

const STYLE = `House style (the owner's): plain wording, sentence case, direct and brief; tables and ranked lists over prose; every number carries its unit and a source link to its evidence file, e.g. [mrms.json](validation-evidence/mrms.json), or "computed: <formula>"; unverified items say "unverified" and why; no "best" claims about providers or libraries (AGENTS.md rule 9); evidence honesty wording (rule 5): observation / satellite estimate / radar estimate / official alert, never damage, "no radar data (meanings unverified)" for MRMS -99 and -999, cloud top only; never write names of AI models or AI vendors into any file; no emoji. In evidence files a "review" key wins over "facts"; mark "unreviewed" where none exists.`

const C = `# Fragment: section 11 → ${FRAG}11-prototype.md (budget 160 lines)
${STYLE}
Read: ${EVID}prototype-globe.json, prototype-mrms.json, prototype-goes.json (including its "acha2kmc" key), prototype-integration.json (including its "fixups" key), webgl-runtime.json ("recipe"), parallax.json, ${REPO}/research/globe/prototype/ (serve.py, globe.js, mrms_volume.py, goes_cloud_height.py, parallax.py docstrings; tests/; fixtures/ provenance), ${EVID}main-architecture.json (the website rules the prototype does not yet follow), and view ${EVID}globe-prototype.png and ${EVID}globe-volume.png.
Write "## 11. Prototype" with: what was built (a table of files with bytes and purpose; where it lives: research/globe/prototype, outside the site); what it proved in a real browser (the measured numbers: canvas non-black fraction, toggle pixel change, 390 px no sideways scroll, CDN-blocked message with the panel intact, hover, offline state "Off", voxel counts equal to panel counts for the synthetic 1,265 and sample 3,931 fixtures, draw timings, test counts 213 unit / 7 browser and their run times); embed both screenshots with one-line captions stating what each shows and that the imagery is a night GeoColor composite over Montana and an archived 2025-06-15 MRMS sample, not live; the MRMS script's measurements (bytes per step for 11 and 33 levels, decode time, output bytes at 20/35/50 dBZ, the event peak step, the Montana -999/-99 shares); the GOES script's measurements for ACHAC and ACHA2KMC (bytes, runtime, latency, valid and DQF shares, p10/p50/p90 heights, the real satellite longitudes read from the files and what they mean for parallax.json; the design point that ACHA2KMC heights at flagged DQF are 20–24% of box cells against 29–30% good); the fix-ups made after integration (per-source freshness from measured latency with the limits used; the Python-first fix moving dBZ steps into serve.py and the voxel format change of about 2.1 bytes per voxel; the stray file); how to run (the exact commands from the docstrings, including the Playwright venv note and the GOES_LIVE=1 switch); what it does NOT prove (GPU frame rates — SwiftShader only; real phones; iOS/Android WebGL2; the vendored three.js route; any accuracy claim); and "### From prototype to the website" — a table mapping each prototype piece to its website equivalent (serve.py endpoints → build.py products in _site/data; CDN Cesium → vendored library; layer panel states → the site's loaded/problem/stale; dark tokens → style.css tokens; fixtures → sample.py SAMPLE data) with the rule each change satisfies.`

const ASSEMBLE = `# Assemble ${README} from the fragments
${STYLE}
Fragments in ${FRAG}: 01-plan.md (title, status paragraph, sections 1–7), 08-sources.md (sections 8 and 13), 09a-rendering.md (section 9 heading and 9a), 09b-architecture.md (9b), 10-pipeline.md (sections 10 and 12), 11-prototype.md (11), 14-questions.md (14), 15-prerequisites.md (15). Also read ${SCRATCH}/supervisor-log.md for the method facts and ${REPO}/docs/DECISIONS.md (its last entry number; a D30 entry recording this research may have been appended by another agent — if it is there, cite it; if not, write "D30 (to be recorded)").
Steps:
1. Build the README in this order: title and status paragraph (from 01), sections 1–7, 8, 9 (9a then 9b under one "## 9." heading), 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, then write section 16 yourself. Split 08 and 10 by their "## " headings to reorder. Keep the fragments' text; do not paraphrase their numbers. Fix only mechanical seams (duplicate headings, a missing blank line before a table, a section number).
2. Renumber the proposed DECISIONS entries consistently: in every fragment the synthesis's proposals are cited as D30–D40 (e.g. "D31", "(D32)", "D33 proposal", "D38", "D39", "D30–D40"). The next real entry in docs/DECISIONS.md is D30 and records this research, so shift the proposals up by one: do the replacement from high to low (D40→D41, then D39→D40, … D30→D31) so nothing is shifted twice; do not touch the real D1–D29 or any "D-G" id; then add one sentence in the status paragraph: "docs/DECISIONS.md D30 records this research; the proposed entries D31–D41 (§9b) wait for Carson." Report the count of replacements per number.
3. Write "## 16. How this was produced and verified" (budget 90 lines): the method (a supervisor set the plan and critiqued; parallel agents did the work: 4 verification workflows over 14 workstreams, each report independently refuted; parallax geometry, predeclared evaluation and hosting facts as separate checks; a 5-stage prototype build with real-browser tests; two design rounds — three desktop-era designs and one website design, six judges across three lenses, two syntheses; a website-architecture map after main was merged; section writers and this critic), the counts, the rules the agents were bound by (rule 7 live content checks, rule 8 browser checks, rule 9 no "best", rule 5 wording), then "### Evidence file index": a table of every file in validation-evidence/ (name, bytes, reviewed yes/no, one-line content) generated from the directory (list it; read each file's top-level keys only), the prototype files, the design-references files; then "### What remains unverified" collected from the fragments' unverified lists (one line each); then "### How to re-run" (the test commands, the prototype commands, the evidence files' "urls_checked" as the re-check list).
4. Checks before you finish: every relative link in the README resolves to a file (write and run a small Python script; list any that do not and fix the link or mark it); headings are "## 1." … "## 16." in order with no duplicates; every table row has the same number of cells as its header (script); no names of AI models or AI vendors anywhere in the file (grep for the common ones and for "Co-Authored"); the branch name may stay; report total lines and bytes. Write the README; do not edit the fragments or any other file. Return: line and byte counts, the renumbering counts, the link-check result, the table-check result, and anything you could not place.`

const CRITIC = `# Adversarial critic of ${README} and the docs edits
${STYLE}
Read ${README} in full; ${REPO}/docs/DECISIONS.md (the last entry, D30, if present) and ${REPO}/docs/ROADMAP.md (the globe item and the schedule note, if present); ${SCRATCH}/supervisor-log.md (the ACCEPT/REJECT verdicts, the architecture shift, the confirmed Actions cadence); ${SCRATCH}/plan-critique-product.json and plan-critique-technical.json; and the evidence files you need to check a number.
Your job is to find what is wrong, missing or inconsistent, and fix the small things in place:
1. Completeness: every workstream W0–W21 has its result in section 5 and its detail somewhere in 8–13; every decision D-G1…D-G26 in section 2 appears in section 14 (or section 14 says why not) with the same id and meaning; the two routes in section 1 match sections 6 and 9b; the proposed entries are numbered D31–D41 everywhere and D30 is this research; section 11 reflects the fix-ups (per-source freshness, Python-first dBZ steps, ACHA2KMC numbers); the owner's screenshots and the OSM Boundary Extractor are covered in 13; the confirmed Actions cadence (four scheduled runs on main in about 9.5 h, gaps 151.5/141.6/264.5 min, measured 2026-10-17 05:50 UTC from the Actions API) appears in sections 1, 6 (P0) or 7 and in ROADMAP.
2. Rules: rule 5 wording everywhere (no "measured cloud-top height", no hail size on reflectivity, no "confirmed", no all-clear; "no radar data (meanings unverified)" for -99/-999; cloud top only; parallax wording verbatim and its 33-vs-34 km note); rule 9 (no "best", no ranking of providers by quality; "recommended by the synthesis" is allowed); rule 6 (null geometry never "no alert"); the site's gap words quoted correctly; no AI model or vendor names (grep).
3. Numbers: spot-check 25 numbers across the sections against their cited evidence file (open the file, find the value); list each as match / mismatch / not found and fix mismatches in the README (never in the evidence files). Pay attention to: GIBS latency range, MRMS bytes per step, voxel counts and bytes at 20/35/50 dBZ, three.js and CesiumJS bytes, first-visit bytes for the two routes, ACHA2KMC shares, Billings elevation, the frame box, the build's 45.7 MB / 3.9 MB, the schedule gaps.
4. Contradictions: the fragments' own contradiction lists (in the writers' outputs; some are repeated in section 16's unverified list) — make sure each is either resolved in the text, carried as "unverified", or listed as an owner question in 14.
5. Form: links resolve (script), tables well-formed (script), headings in order, no duplicate section numbers, the status paragraph is accurate (research only; nothing ships; branch; PR #2; main merged).
Fix small faults directly in the README (wording, a number, a link, a missing row). For anything larger, do not rewrite: list it. Then run: cd ${REPO} && python -m unittest discover -s tests 2>&1 | tail -1 (expect OK). Write ${EVID}critic-report.json (at most 20 KB): {"checked_at_utc", "fixed": [{"where", "what"}], "not_fixed": [{"where", "what", "why"}], "numbers_checked": [{"number", "section", "evidence_file", "result"}], "rule_findings": [...], "completeness_findings": [...], "readme_lines", "readme_bytes", "links_broken": [...], "tables_malformed": [...]} and return its summary as your final text.`

log('Final writing pass: section 11, then assembly, then the critic')
const c = await agent(C, { label: 'write:11-prototype', phase: 'Prototype section', model: WORKER })
const a = await agent(ASSEMBLE, { label: 'assemble:README', phase: 'Assemble', model: WORKER })
const k = await agent(CRITIC, { label: 'critic', phase: 'Critic', model: WORKER })
return { section11: c, assembly: a, critic: k }

Notes for the assembler:
- 159 lines, within the 160 budget. ASCII only, no AI model or vendor names, and every relative link resolves from `research/globe/`. Nothing in the repo was changed or committed.
- The "213 unit / 7 browser" count is 213 in total: 206 offline tests plus the 7 browser cases. I re-ran the four offline modules for this section (83, 55, 56 and 12 tests, all OK).
- The 2.1 bytes per voxel figure checks out: 2.10 on the sample fixture and 2.09 on the synthetic one, measured by re-running `serve.dbz_step_index` on the fixtures.
- Both screenshots predate the fix-ups, so they show the old 15-minute GOES limit. The section says so and marks re-capture as not done.
- `parallax.py` still uses -75.2 for GOES-East, and `parallax.json` was not re-tabled. The section states the -75.0 correction and its 0.17 km effect.
- The browser file and the full suite were not re-run for this section. Those numbers come from `prototype-integration.json`, and the section marks them that way.
- The site's map script is at `website/static/map/map.js`, not `website/static/map.js`.
result.assembly:
README written to `/home/user/RoofingApp/research/globe/README.md`. It is the only changed file (uncommitted; the old 12,862-byte version is overwritten and remains in git history).

**Size:** 1,250 lines, 225,843 bytes. §16 is 139 lines against the 90-line budget. The 39-file index plus four group rows (about 45 lines) and the 26-item unverified list account for most of it. I kept both whole rather than cut rows.

**Renumbering:** D30–D40 became D31–D41 in one pass, 61 replacements in the plan (§1–§7), §9b, §14 and §15. Per old number: D30 9, D31 4, D32 8, D33 9, D34 4, D35 6, D36 2, D37 1, D38 5, D39 5, D40 8. D1–D29 and all D-G ids are untouched. D30 already exists in `docs/DECISIONS.md` (commit ea265ad), so I cited it and added the required sentence.

**Link check:** 457 relative targets, 0 missing. Seven are directory links (`validation-evidence/`, `prototype/`, `prototype/tests/`, `prototype/fixtures/`, `design-references/`) and exist. No external or anchor links.

**Table check:** 45 tables, 459 body rows. Every row matches its header's cell count, and each table has a blank line before it.

**Headings:** one H1; `## 1.` to `## 16.` in order; no duplicate headings.

**Names and emoji:** no AI model or vendor names, no Co-Authored line, no emoji. One hit: `codex` in the branch name in the status line, which the brief allows.

**Checks run at assembly:** repo `python -m unittest discover -s tests` gave 223 OK; `desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload` gave PASS; prototype `test_serve` 83, `test_mrms_volume` 55 and `test_parallax` 12 passed; parallax self-check 9 of 9. The browser test file was not re-run.

**Changes beyond the mechanical list (please check):**
1. Status paragraph: the fragment-only sentence "Nothing in this fragment edits DECISIONS.md or ROADMAP.md…" is replaced by the required sentence.
2. ROADMAP line citations: 21 shifted to the current `docs/ROADMAP.md`, per the supervisor's post-critic list. I matched each old line to the same content in the new file. My first pass missed the three in §10; they are fixed in the final build.
3. Folium row (§9b, D38): marked "recorded in D30; not a new entry" rather than dropped, so numbering stays D31–D41. The "wait for Carson" sentence therefore does not cover D38.
4. §14 row 17: the critic's citation is kept, with "(line 113 in the current file)" added.

**Could not place, left as written:**
- §1 item 6 and the W14 row give 186 prototype tests; the final count is 213 (§11). §16 notes this.
- §1 item 5 and §7 give measured schedule gaps of 151.5, 141.6 and 264.5 min (median 151.5). §9b and §14 give a median of 146.5–151.5 min (judge2-engineering K1). I did not reconcile them.
- Several notes cite files outside the repo (plan critiques, the supervisor log). §16 says so.
- The supervisor's "2.5 to 4.5 hours" item is not in any fragment, so nothing changed.

Build scripts (scratchpad, not in the repo): `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-RoofingApp/7638440a-a008-5ef8-a289-86be0a23e7a7/scratchpad/readme-build/assemble.py`, `sec16.py`, `checks.py`. Rebuild and check with `python3 -I assemble.py && python3 -I checks.py`.
result.critic:
Critic pass on `research/globe/README.md` is done. The repo suite passes (`Ran 223 tests, OK`). Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Report:** `/home/user/RoofingApp/research/globe/validation-evidence/critic-report.json` (19,645 bytes, valid JSON, no AI model or vendor names).

**README:** 1,252 lines, 228,569 bytes after 47 exact-match edits. Links: 460 occurrences, 69 unique, 0 broken. Tables: 0 malformed. Headings 1–16 in order.

**Fixed (37 entries), main ones:**
- Cadence: four starts span 9.3 h, not "about 9.5 h"; time given as 05:13Z and 05:50 UTC; stale 146.5 median replaced by 151.5 over three gaps (P0, §10, §14 row 26).
- three.js gzip 417,073 B was cited to `globe-libs.json`, which lacks it. Now cited to `design-synthesis-website.json`.
- §1 said observation and satellite estimate were AGENTS rule 5 kinds. Rule 5 names five other kinds; the two are marked proposed (D33).
- Datum: "above sea level" and "geopotential, referenced to the geoid" were stated as fact while §8 says the datum is open. Now attributed to the CF text and unconfirmed.
- Parallax legend in Table 2 made verbatim (exact match in `parallax.json`).
- Test count 186 updated to 206 offline plus 7 browser; first-frame 91 ms corrected to 95 ms.
- Stale citations: AGENTS rule 7 and rule 6 line numbers; D7 corrected to D12; Benchland is ROADMAP item 11.
- "no Chromium on the research machine" contradicted the Chromium 141 runs; replaced.
- Basemap "built by hand" contradicted the existing `tools/build_basemap.py`.
- Overture 470 footprints qualified: 464 inside the 1 km box.
- Prototype square-degree area corrected to 83.03.
- Map gap words: a second phrase, "No radar data on this map", is at `map.js:36`.
- `docs/` changes now stated; a vendor-named branch segment in the status line and §16 replaced by an ellipsis.
- Added a D-G1…D-G26 → §14 row map; reworded a stale §14 question (ROADMAP item 16 exists).

**Not fixed (11), main ones:**
- `docs/ROADMAP.md` top line and D27 still say "every 10 minutes": owner's call.
- D38 kept as a marked row so D31–D41 numbering holds; the supervisor asked to drop it.
- Older text in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md` names AI vendors. It is outside this research's edits.
- Two decode timings (20.6–23.0 s and 17.3–18.6 s) are not reconciled; both come from different runs.
- "685,194 B" first-visit figure is not a literal in the evidence; components sum to about 0.69 MB.
- Judge score values were not located by text search. "30.09%" was not found as a literal.
- ACHA datum and HT units (metres or feet) and the GOES newest-day conflict (2025/097 vs 2025/166) need data checks.

**Numbers:** 42 checked. Matches: MRMS bytes, voxel counts and bytes at 20/35/50 dBZ, library and CesiumJS bytes, crops, build totals, frame box, Billings elevation, schedule gaps. Mismatches were fixed. The writers' fragments have no headed contradiction lists. The critic used the §8 corrections, the §8/§16 unverified lists, §12 conflicts and the supervisor's conflict note instead.
